newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Petrobras seen strong after oil sector open.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Petrobras seen strong after oil sector open.

text.p: Brazil's state-owned oil giant Petrobras will remain the dominant player in the Brazilian oil sector even after it is opened to private competition, according to senior oil company officials.
"Petrobras will continue to be for a long time a player with a significant capacity to dominate the market," said Joao Geraldo Piquet Carneiro, director of oil firm Ipiranga, at a seminar in Rio.
"The government model only allows for a very slow introduction of competition into the oil sector," he added.

He said under government plans for breaking up the state oil monopoly Petrobras would initially not only retain control over all its existing assets, but would even expand its activities in conjunction with new private partners.
The director of oil company Azevedo Travassos Petroleo, Jose Eduardo Jardim, believes it is not in anyone's interest to weaken Petrobras when they can benefit from the company's expertise in Brazil.

"Petrobras will remain strong. No one is interested in weakening Petrobras even less so foreign investors," Jardim said. "Petrobras knows Brazil, it has worked in Brazil for many years. Petrobras is extremely competent."
Carneiro said it was "absolutely essential" under these circumstances that the future regulator of the oil sector, the National Petroleum Agency (ANP), be wholly independent in its decision making.
"The regulator's independence is fundamental for containing the company's power of monopoly and for ensuring that a minimum of competition is gradually introduced into the market," Carneiro said.
Carneiro and Jardim favored plans to locate the ANP in Rio de Janeiro, saying it would be the best place for recruiting qualified staff for the ANP given that Petrobras is also headquartered in Rio.
In August, Brazil's lower house of Congress started hearings on a first draft of a bill which would lay down the rules of opening up the oil and gas sector.
